question.explanation:
To solve the equation $\sqrt{-3x-8} = x+2,$ we raise both sides to the power of $2.$ This allows us to get rid of the radical, and gives us a quadratic equation that is easier to solve:

\begin{align} \sqrt{-3x-8} & = x+2\\[3pt] \left(\sqrt{-3x-8}\right)^2 &= (x+2)^2\\[3pt] -3x-8 & = x^2+4x+4\\[3pt] x^2 + 7x + 12 & = 0\\[3pt] (x^2 +4x) + (3x + 12) & = 0\\[3pt] x(x+4) + 3(x+4) & = 0\\[3pt] (x+3)(x+4) & = 0\\[3pt] x & = -4,\, -3 \end{align}

Remember that in square root equations, we should always check the obtained value(s) to ensure that they are actually solutions of the original equation.

  • First, we check whether the obtained value $x=-4$ is a solution of the original equation:

\begin{align} \sqrt{-3(-4)-8} & \overset{?}{=} -4+2\\[3pt] \sqrt{4} & \overset{?}{=} -2\\[3pt] 2 & \neq -2 \quad \color{red}\times \end{align}

The value $x=-4$ does not satisfy the original equation, so we discard it.

  • Second, we check whether the obtained value $x=-3$ is a solution of the original equation:

\begin{align} \sqrt{-3(-3)-8} & \overset{?}{=} -3+2\\[3pt] \sqrt{1} & \overset{?}{=} -1\\[3pt] 1 & \neq -1 \quad \color{red}\times \end{align} The value $x=-3$ does not satisfy the original equation, so we discard it.

Therefore, there is no solution to $\sqrt{-3x-8} = x+2x.$

question.explanation:
To solve the equation $\sqrt{5x-9} = x-1,$ we raise both sides to the power of $2.$ This allows us to get rid of the radical, and gives us a quadratic equation that is easier to solve:

\begin{align} \sqrt{5x - 9} & = x - 1\\[3pt] \left(\sqrt{5x - 9}\right)^2 &= (x - 1)^2\\[3pt] 5x - 9 & = x^2 - 2x + 1\\[3pt] x^2 - 7 x + 10 & = 0\\[3pt] (x^2 - 2x) + (-5x + 10) & = 0\\[3pt] x(x - 2) - 5(x - 2) & = 0\\[3pt] (x-5)(x-2) & = 0\\[3pt] x & = 2,\, 5 \end{align}

Remember that in square root equations, we should always check the obtained value(s) to ensure that they are actually solutions of the original equation.

  • First, we check whether the obtained value $x=2$ is a solution of the original equation:

\begin{align} \sqrt{5(2)-9} & \overset{?}{=} 2-1\\[3pt] \sqrt{1} & \overset{?}{=} 1\\[3pt] 1 & = 1 \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align} Indeed, the value $x=2$ does satisfy the original equation.

  • Second, we check whether the obtained value $x=5$ is a solution of the original equation:

\begin{align} \sqrt{5(5)-9} & \overset{?}{=} 5-1\\[3pt] \sqrt{16} & \overset{?}{=} 4\\[3pt] 4 & = 4 \quad \color{green}\checkmark \end{align}

Indeed, the value $x=5$ does satisfy the original equation.

Therefore, the solutions of $\sqrt{5x-9} = x-1$ are $x=2,\,5.$

question.explanation:
Squaring both sides of the equation, we get

\begin{align} \sqrt{2 - 3x} & = 2\\[5pt] \left(\sqrt{2 - 3x}\right)^2 & = 2^2\\[5pt] 2 - 3x & = 4\\[5pt] 3x & = -2\\[5pt] x & = -\dfrac{2}{3}. \end{align}

Let's check the result by plugging it into the original equation: \begin{align} \require{cancel} \sqrt{2 - 3\left( -\dfrac{2}{3} \right)} & \overset{?}{=} 2 \\[5pt] \sqrt{2 - \cancel{3}\left( -\dfrac{2}{\cancel{3}} \right)} & \overset{?}{=} 2 \\[5pt] \sqrt{2 - (-2)} & \overset{?}{=} 2 \\[5pt] \sqrt{2 + 2} & \overset{?}{=} 2 \\[5pt] \sqrt{4} & \overset{?}{=} 2 \\[5pt] 2 & = 2\;\; {\color{green}\checkmark} \end{align}

The value $x = -\dfrac{2}{3}$ satisfies the original equation, so we can accept it as a solution.

Therefore, the solution to $\sqrt{2 - 3x} = 2$ is $x = -\dfrac{2}{3}.$
